entries.title: Read-poverty and the information floor
entries.one_breath: A human overseeing a fleet of software agents reads digests, not transcripts, and any digest that guarantees catching all k load-bearing artifacts among N while opening only m must carry at least log2 C(N,k) - log2 C(m,k) bits.

sections: S2 (sec:floor), Theorem 1
S6 Read-poverty (sec:readpoverty / sec:lowerbound), "Legibility lower bound with a review budget" -- explicitly "Theorem 1 of the companion formal paper"

entries.title: Split-digest theorem (comonotone characterization)
entries.one_breath: A scalar head serves a reader iff ranking by it realizes that reader's optimal selection at every budget; one head serves two readers iff their preference orders are comonotone, and the successor and operator readers provably are not.

sections: S3 (sec:split), Theorem 2
S7.3 Discovery/Relevance (sec:relevance), "No universal monotone identification of the two heads" -- stated as an instance of paper1's comonotone characterization
S8.2 Tokens (sec:tokens-digest), "The Split-Digest Theorem" -- successor-vs-operator compaction heads, explicitly the other instance of the same theorem

entries.title: The derived regret head
entries.one_breath: Inspect iff C_miss(x)*a(x) >= c_att + C_fa*(1-a(x)); the folklore ranking key stakes x irreversibility x anomaly is the Bayes-optimal surfacing rule iff anomaly is a calibrated posterior.

sections: S4 (sec:regret), Theorem 3
S5.1 The operator (sec:sdt), "The SDT-spined attention objective"
S7.3 Discovery/Relevance (sec:relevance), "Decision-theoretic derivation of the regret head" -- explicitly a popularization of paper1's "The regret head is derived, not designed"

entries.title: Digest-zoom Pareto frontier and the zoom-advantage theorem
entries.one_breath: A two-constraint rate-distortion program R(delta,f) prices misses separately from flag rate with a closed form for Bernoulli sources, and adaptive halving finds the k criticals inside F flagged items in at most 2k*ceil(log2(F/k))+4k group opens versus F flat.

sections: S5 (sec:frontier): S5.1 the pinned-joint proposition, S5.2 Theorem 4 (zoom advantage)
S6 Read-poverty (sec:lowerbound), "The other half of the price: zoom is cheap" -- restates the zoom theorem's bound and the F=2500,k=10 worked numbers under the same theorem label used for R1

entries.title: Hypervisor enforceability = supervisory control
entries.one_breath: A safety policy is regimentable (preventable pre-effect) by an agent hypervisor iff it is controllable in the Ramadge-Wonham sense with respect to the uncontrollable event set; gate the channel, never the token.

sections: S5 (sec:theorem), boxed "Theorem (Regimentation = controllability)"; restated as Theorem 2 in paper4.tex S4 (sec:p2) as Pillar II of the Sealed Harbor

"Synchronous State Decidability -- closing OP-2" (thm:decidability) is the special case Sigma_c={DB writes}; the general theorem is folded as "The general boundary: regimentation is controllability" (sec:controllability, thm:regimentation-controllability) with the nine-policy table (tab:policy-classification), the gate-the-channel case, partial observation, and exercises ex:swk-classify-two, ex:swk-synthesis

entries.title: Sheaf verdict: cohomology of equivocation
entries.one_breath: In gossip of signed logs, the least-squares completion residual detects a single equivocator's split-view lie beyond pairwise comparison iff the unchecked edge lies on a cycle of the visible coordinate subgraph, and its endpoints' reports are relayed to the analyst.

sections: S4 (sec:mechanism), boxed "Theorem 1 (mechanism)"; harness verdict COMMIT in S5 (sec:harness)
S(fh-sheaf), "Detection iff the missing edge closes a visible cycle" -- explicit restatement citing "the companion paper on the cohomology of equivocation"

entries.title: Inspection tower: reputation is amortized verification
entries.one_breath: A bonded judge is deterred iff rho*d*B >= G; auditors sampled sealed from C disjoint cliques make bribery all-or-nothing and unprofitable below corrupt value C*B, so finite bond capital certifies a tower of logarithmic depth, and lifetime audit spend falls from Theta(T) to Theta(log T) or O(1) as reputation accumulates.

sections: S4 (sec:stage) Theorem (Stage deterrence); S5 (sec:tower) Theorem (Tower contraction); S6 (sec:amort) Theorem (Amortization)
S(sec:oracle) The grading oracle's incentive-compatibility, "Tower contraction; imported from the companion paper" -- verbatim restatement of paper3.tex's Theorem tower-contraction

entries.title: The work-unit machine
entries.one_breath: The state machine (phase, policy, receipt, epoch/holder/stale-token, grants-with-parentage, effect journal, idempotency journal, settlement) satisfies six safety invariants in all 536 reachable states, each guard shown load-bearing by mutation.

sections: "The work unit, model-checked" (sec:workunit): the six invariants as a Model-checked property (thm:workunit), the shortest-crime table (tab:workunit-crimes), exercises ex:swk-crimes and ex:swk-seventh-invariant

entries.title: Sealed-room noninterference
entries.one_breath: With declared release g(s) = s mod 2, Erin's observations are identical whenever g(s)=g(s') for every interleaving, and may differ only at explicit gate-release steps otherwise -- noninterference modulo declassification, verified exhaustively to depth 7 on the finite clean-room model.

sections: S3 (sec:p1), boxed "Theorem 1 (noninterference modulo declassification; finite model, exhaustive)", Pillar I

entries.title: Epsilon-conservation of the release ledger
entries.one_breath: The release ledger's only spending transition atomically appends the record and adds the spend, so every reachable state satisfies sigma = sum of the ledger's epsilons and sigma <= epsilon_max, including under concurrent invocation.

sections: S5 (sec:p3), boxed "Theorem 3 (epsilon-conservation)", Pillar III

entries.title: Canary detection power and SPRT latency
entries.one_breath: Independent per-canary misses turn k smuggled canaries into detection probability 1 - beta^k; Wald's sequential probability ratio test against the permutation null turns leak intensity into an expected time-to-detection with realized error rates at or below target.

sections: S6 (sec:p4), boxed "Theorem 4a (power)" and "Theorem 4b (latency, Wald)", Pillar IV

entries.title: No-mint reputation inheritance
entries.one_breath: Discount-and-split as transfer -- the child receives a discounted, debited share of each source's spend -- keeps total live creditable reputation below total witnessed value under any sequence of forks, merges, chains, or re-derivation cycles.

sections: S2 (sec:nomint), boxed "Theorem 1 (no-mint)"

S(sec:continuity) Continuity is a personal-identity problem, "Status" note after Exercise (3) -- "an executed no-mint theorem (research-ledger item A6)", full transfer-semantics restatement with the same 8.2x copy-fork exhibit

entries.title: Engine substitution and resurrection soundness
entries.one_breath: Unattested, the period-2 price never depends on the actual engine so swapping to a cheap one always pays; daemon-attested engine ids flip the incentive to the planner's efficiency rule at zero audit stake, and sanction-respecting reputation survives provider migration under three named clauses, each individually load-bearing.

sections: S3 (sec:engine), boxed "Theorem 2a"/"Theorem 2b (the IC flip)"; S4 (sec:resurrection), boxed "Theorem 3 (resurrection soundness)" and its scope Lemma, which names the migration soundness property "Def. III.6.1"

S(sec:identity) Identity: the root the whole chain hangs from -- "Sanction-respecting reputation" (the Def. III.6.1 that paper5.tex's Theorem 3 names), and its subsection sec:body-behind-name "The body behind the name: engine swaps and resurrection", which restates Theorems 2a/2b as the labeled claim thm:engine-swap (Theorem, with proof) and Theorem 3 with its scope lemma as thm:resurrection-soundness (Model-checked property), with the worked numbers in a pdexample and the two-period/bounded-check limits in a pdboundary.

entries.title: Costly-escalation threshold equilibrium and the debit tuning band
entries.one_breath: A strictly increasing escalation payoff gives a unique separating threshold u*(delta); the feasible debit set between the alarm-fatigue wall and the distress-silencing wall is an interval that can be empty, in which case the honest fix is capacity or evidence quality, not tuning.

sections: S5.4 Human-in-the-loop escalation (sec:escalation) and S7.5 quality gates (sec:gates) -- "crying wolf has a price" costly-signal design, cited inline as "item R14 of the research ledger"

entries.title: Queueing specialization boundary and the succession price
entries.one_breath: Sole ownership weakly dominates the pool iff the skill premium clears the exact Erlang-C boundary g_A(rho,c), falsifying the whitepaper's proposed threshold in both directions; with mortality and succession, pooling dominates at every skill premium once xi/eta exceeds D* = etaK/(1-etaK).

sections: S(sec:thm-boundary / sec:queue), boxed "Theorem 2 (queueing specialization boundary)"; S(sec:succession), boxed "Theorem 3 (price of the succession rule)"

S4.3 Sole-responsibility roles (sec:sole-roles), "Queueing Specialization Boundary" -- annotated \Verified--corrected, citing "the companion formal paper's Theorem 2" by name, same g(rho,2)=1+2rho-rho^2 closed form

entries.title: Context paging with an untrusted pin oracle
entries.one_breath: Landlord's k/(k-h+1) competitiveness against offline OPT imports to variable-size context spans; a pin oracle corrupted on a psi fraction of consultations costs only an additive, linear psi*N*c_refetch penalty under repair-on-touch, sharing its corruption budget with R1's forgeable-feature budget.

sections: S8.3 Context paging (sec:context-paging), "Context Paging Competitiveness" -- annotated \Verified--upgraded from proposed, with the b9_context_paging.py sweep numbers

entries.title: Tractable deontic-conflict fragment and its NP-complete frontier
entries.one_breath: Inside a fragment of facts, definite Horn rules, ground deontic O/F rules, exclusive interval claims and difference constraints, conflict detection is polynomial and witness-producing; one expressive step out (disjunctive obligations under discharge choice) makes conflict-freedom NP-complete.

sections: S(sec:lang / sec:thm-detect), boxed "Theorem 1a (membership)" and "Theorem 1b (frontier: one step outside is NP-complete)"

entries.title: Consistency radius of the completion residual (CR-1/2/3)
entries.one_breath: The completion residual r is a certified lower bound on any injected lie (equality at the completion, closed form r = |s| * sqrt(1 - R_eff) for a single-edge lie), localizes to visible cycles through the equivocator, and computes as at most L scalar graph-Laplacian solves.

sections: S6 (sec:radius), boxed "Theorem CR-1 (soundness and achievability)", "Theorem CR-2 (localization)", "Theorem CR-3 (complexity)"

entries.title: The probation cliff (front-loaded newcomer restriction)
entries.one_breath: Among all newcomer-restriction schedules with equal power to deter a short-horizon whitewasher, the maximally front-loaded feasible one -- a cliff, not a ramp -- uniquely minimizes the tax on honest newcomers.

sections: S5 (sec:cliff), boxed "Theorem 4 (the probation cliff)"

S(sec:identity) Identity: the root the whole chain hangs from, "Front-loaded probation dominance, under a ceiling" -- annotated "the whitepaper statement of the companion paper's probation-cliff theorem", "carried as item B6 of the research ledger"

entries.title: Claim-signaling incentive compatibility (mechanized discount-factor thresholds)
entries.one_breath: In the corrected claim-signaling stage game, a grim trigger is subgame-perfect iff delta >= 1/3 and a three-round graduated trigger iff delta exceeds the unique real root delta* = 0.3425080314 of 2*delta^3+2*delta^2+2*delta-1=0, both mechanically checked by Z3 and TLA+/Apalache.

sections: S7 (sec:signaling), "The discount-factor connection: claim signaling, mechanized"
